The Heaven effects are unstable in the game: a stripe placed over objects will either catch obstacles it should not or break off halfway. The rules below keep that from happening.
Clear 4 columns before the stripe and 4 after it, then extend it 4 cells forward. An empty column is a column with no blocks, spikes or pits.
The room at the start keeps the effect from catching obstacles placed before the stripe, and the margin at the end lets the last objects sink all the way.
Example: a stripe of 6 cells with 4 empty columns on each side. Extended forward it takes 10 cells.
The stripe must be at least 10 cells long: that is how much one column takes to rise, about 0.8 seconds. Every extra cell adds one more column, so 11 cells give two, 12 give three and so on.

The effect starts and ends on obstacles, not on its own. The column where the stripe begins must not be empty. Clear 9 columns after the stripe, extend it over them and place any object on the next column: that object is what stops the effect.
Example: a stripe of 14 cells, with its first column occupied and the one past its end occupied too. Five columns will rise in full.

A set of fixes and extra features for The Impossible Game. Changes go into the game executable, and the original state can be restored at any time.
F1 toggles invulnerability right during play. Handy when testing hard levels.
If a level folder holds custom graphics and audio, the game loads those instead of the built in ones. F2 switches resources during play. Jump physics is taken from level.ini in the level folder.
Removes the false medal message on the first run of a level. Other medal messages are left alone.
Opens the levels folder right away when a custom level is chosen in the game menu.
Makes up for the music lagging behind the level on the first try by holding the level start and matching the sound with later tries.
Stops the game window from being stretched when the Windows interface scale is above 100%.

Jump physics is not the same across the original levels. You can change it for your own level, and the values will be saved to level.ini in its folder. Without the patch the game does not read that file and ignores custom values.
Hold Alt and press the left mouse button on the grid to show the guide for the chosen physics.
